links.outcome: Reading grade level of LLM responses (FKGL) to lipedema questions
links.effect: Perplexity FKGL 12.80 ± 2.10, significantly higher than ChatGPT-5o (p = .041) and Gemini-3 (p = .036); authors note barrier for limited e-health literacy.
links.quote: In readability analyses, Perplexity (12.80 ± 2.10) required a significantly higher educational level according to FKGL scores compared to both ChatGPT-5o (p = .041) and Gemini-3 (p = .036).

links.outcome: Reference reliability and hallucination tendencies in LLM citations
links.effect: ChatGPT-5o outperformed Perplexity in source verifiability (p = .031), bibliographic precision (p = .044), and total RHS scores (p = .027).
links.quote: Regarding reference reliability, ChatGPT-5o outperformed Perplexity in source verifiability (p = .031), bibliographic precision (p = .044), and total RHS scores (p = .027), emerging as the most robust model in this domain.

screen.reason: The study empirically benchmarks three LLMs (ChatGPT-5o, Gemini-3, Perplexity AI) on 30 clinical guideline questions for lipedema, assessing accuracy, readability, and reference reliability without testing a specific organizational deployment practice.
